# Finding the Antiderivative of ∫ log(x) dx

## Integration by Parts

I'll use the integration by parts formula: ∫ u dv = u*v - ∫ v du

Let:
- u = log(x), so du = (1/x) dx
- dv = dx, so v = x

## Applying the Formula

∫ log(x) dx = x * log(x) - ∫ x * (1/x) dx

Simplify the remaining integral:

∫ x * (1/x) dx = ∫ 1 dx = x

## Combining Results

∫ log(x) dx = x * log(x) - x + C

## Verification

Let me differentiate the result to confirm:
- d/dx [x * log(x) - x] = log(x) + x * (1/x) - 1 = log(x) + 1 - 1 = log(x) ✓

<answer>x*log(x) - x + C</answer>
